title: IPL Business Value Rockets Past $20 Billion as Franchise Sales Hit Record Highs
excerpt: Houlihan Lokey's 2026 valuation study pegs the league at $20.6 billion, with Royal Challengers Bengaluru becoming the first cricket team to cross $300 million in brand value.
body:
• The IPL's business value has risen 11.4% to $20.6 billion, marking a second straight year of double-digit growth, according to Houlihan Lokey's 2026 valuation study.
  • Royal Challengers Bengaluru became the first cricket team in the world to surpass $300 million in brand value, reaching $312 million after a 16% jump.
  • Record-breaking franchise transactions — RCB sold for $1.78 billion and Rajasthan Royals for $1.65 billion — drew institutional heavyweights including Blackstone, the Mittal family, and the Aditya Birla Group.
  • Connected TV viewership surged 26% year-on-year during the 2026 season, even as linear television ratings declined nearly 19%, reflecting a shift in how fans consume cricket.

The Indian Premier League has crossed another commercial milestone. The world's richest Twenty20 cricket competition is now worth $20.6 billion, up 11.4% from $18.5 billion a year earlier, according to a new valuation study from U.S.-based investment bank Houlihan Lokey.

It is the second consecutive year the IPL has posted double-digit growth in business value, placing it among a small group of global sports properties expanding rapidly at scale. On a per-match basis, only the NFL generates more commercial value.

Franchise Transactions Reshape Ownership

Two landmark ownership changes during the year turbocharged investor confidence. A consortium comprising Blackstone, Bolt Ventures, the Aditya Birla Group, and the Times of India Group acquired Royal Challengers Bengaluru for a league-record $1.78 billion — the most expensive single franchise transaction in IPL history.

Separately, the Mittal family and Adar Poonawalla — the Serum Institute of India chief who became a household name during the pandemic vaccine rollout — purchased the Rajasthan Royals for $1.65 billion.

"Franchise valuations have reached new highs, private capital participation has accelerated, and the league's commercial ecosystem continues to diversify."

— Harsh Talikoti, Director, Houlihan Lokey Financial and Valuation Advisory

The entry of investors including Blackstone, ArcelorMittal, and the Serum Institute signals that the IPL's appeal now extends well beyond traditional sports owners, according to the report. Private equity firms in the United States and Europe are also showing growing interest in the league's long-term prospects.

RCB Tops the Brand Rankings

Reigning back-to-back champions Bengaluru retained their position as the IPL's most valuable franchise. Their brand value climbed 16% from $269 million to $312 million, making RCB the first cricket team in the world to breach the $300 million mark.

Mumbai Indians ranked second with a brand value of $264 million, up 9.1% from $242 million. Kolkata Knight Riders held third place at $245 million, while Chennai Super Kings came in fourth at $244 million — a comparatively modest 3.8% increase year-on-year.

The IPL's stand-alone brand value also grew, climbing 10.3% to $4.3 billion and adding more than $1.1 billion in brand equity since 2023.

Viewership Shifts to Connected TV

The 2026 season reflected a significant change in consumption habits. JioStar reported a cumulative reach of 1.06 billion screens, but the composition of that audience is evolving. Connected TV viewership rose 26% year-on-year, while linear television ratings dropped 18.8%.

Total league revenues crossed $1.8 billion during the season, underpinned by long-term media rights agreements, sponsorship deals, and a salary cap system that helps franchises maintain profitability.

What This Means for Cricket's Global Future

The Houlihan Lokey report frames the IPL's trajectory as part of a broader trend: cricket's evolution into a globally owned, institutionally backed asset class. The league's combination of audience scale — India alone has over 1.4 billion people — predictable revenue streams, and diversifying commercial opportunities makes it attractive to the same caliber of capital that flows into NFL, Premier League, and Formula 1 franchises.

For the Indian diaspora, the IPL's rising profile carries additional significance. As global investors pour billions into Indian cricket, the league strengthens its position as a cultural export that connects millions abroad to sporting traditions back home. The question now is whether the IPL can sustain this growth trajectory as it approaches the same valuation territory as established Western sports leagues.
